name: SIAI-Marchetti SF.260
summary: Italian aerobatic trainer with a six-cylinder Lycoming and retractable tricycle gear, used by air forces around the world and by civil display teams; many ex-military examples now fly privately in the US.

wings: Low, straight, tapered wing with a thin section
Permanent tip tanks on the wing tips
engines: Single flat-six with a two-blade propeller
Sleek, narrow cowl that flows smoothly into the canopy
fuselage: Long bubble canopy with two or three seats under one sliding canopy
Slim fuselage with a long dorsal spine behind the canopy
Retractable tricycle gear, with the nose gear folding aft
tail: Straight-edged, moderately swept fin with a dorsal fillet
Horizontal tailplane mounted low on the rear fuselage

tellTales: Tip tanks on a small low-wing aerobatic trainer with a sleek bubble canopy
Retractable tricycle gear and a long, swept fin
Slim pencil-like fuselage with a long smooth canopy

confusedWith.howToTell: The P-Mentor has fixed spatted gear, no tip tanks and a Rotax nose; the SF.260 has retractable gear, tip tanks and a six-cylinder cowl.
The PC-7 has a turboprop nose, a taller fuselage and no tip tanks; the SF.260 has a piston nose and tip tanks.
The S-211 is a jet with a shoulder wing and a turbofan; the SF.260 is a low-wing piston airplane with tip tanks.
The T-34 has no tip tanks and a larger, heavier look; the SF.260 is smaller with tip tanks and retractable gear.
